Member: Reese Foster

Blue Cross of Idaho retains the right to add to, delete from and otherwise modify this policy in accordance with our provider contracts Policy Inquiry and Appeals Process Overview This policy outlines the rights available to in-network and out-of-network providers to challenge pre-service and post-service benefit decisions. Contractual appeal rights are not available to out-of-network providers that do not contract directly with Blue Cross of Idaho (“out-of-network”). In-network providers may exercise appeal rights set forth in their contracts with Blue Cross of Idaho. Definitions Request for reconsideration – a provider’s timely pre-service written request for reconsideration of Blue Cross of Idaho’s pre-service benefit denial of the provider’s request for prior authorization (PA). Peer-to-peer call – a provider’s timely request for an informal phone call with a Blue Cross of Idaho medical director or pharmacist to discuss the circumstances and basis for the PA request and denial and provide additional context and clarifying information related to the request, as necessary. Inquiry – a timely post-service request for information regarding the processing of a claim made through Blue Cross of Idaho’s provider portal. An inquiry is distinct from an appeal and does not alter or extend appeal deadlines. Appeal – a timely post-service written request submitted on the appropriate appeal form found on Blue Cross of Idaho’s provider portal, which asks Blue Cross of Idaho to change a prior claim determination for reasons authorized in the provider’s contract and this policy. I. Pre-service Reconsideration Rights 1. Requests for a peer-to-peer call Providers who have questions or information related to an initial benefit determination are encouraged to request a provider-to-provider phone call before submitting a written request for reconsideration so that both the Blue Cross of Idaho medical director who made the initial determination and the treating provider have additional information before a request for reconsideration is considered. One provider-to-provider phone call may be requested within five (5) business days of the original pre-service denial. A provider may also file a written pre-service request for reconsideration. Provider-to-provider calls with a Blue Cross of Idaho physician or other appropriate reviewer related to adverse PA determinations may be submitted to Healthcare Operations at Peer2PeerRequests@bcidaho.com or 888-970-0661 within five (5) business days of the original authorization denial to ensure current treatment needs are reviewed. Supporting clinical information must also be submitted. Provider-to-provider reviews are only available for determinations involving medical judgment (e.g., medical necessity, investigational) and are not available for adverse determinations related to member contract or benefit exclusions. For provider-to-provider discussions about inpatient concurrent reviews, please contact Peer2PeerRequests@bcidaho.com or 888-970-0661 while the member is currently hospitalized. Provider-to-provider discussions are not available once the member is discharged. 2. Pre-service requests for reconsideration of a benefit denial Standard request for reconsideration Providers may submit a written request for reconsideration of a pre-service denial for services, an admission to a facility or a decision by Blue Cross of Idaho during its concurrent review within fifteen (15) business days of the original authorization denial. Reconsideration requests will be responded to by Blue Cross of Idaho within fifteen (15) business days of receipt. Note: If the reconsideration request is submitted untimely, it will be rejected by Blue Cross of Idaho and returned to the provider. After Blue Cross of Idaho has responded to or rejected a provider’s standard request for reconsideration, there are no additional pre-service reconsideration rights available for the requested service. Expedited request for reconsideration An expedited request for reconsideration of a pre-service denial is available only in specific circumstances, and only when submitted within three (3) business days of the original authorization denial for urgent services. Expedited reconsideration requests will be reviewed by a Blue Cross of Idaho medical director, or designee, and a decision on the expedited reconsideration shall be provided no later than three (3) business days following Blue Cross of Idaho’s receipt of the expedited reconsideration request. An expedited request for reconsideration is valid only when there is a delay in medical care or treatment: Could seriously jeopardize the life or health of the member or the member’s ability to regain maximum function, based on a prudent layperson’s judgment, or In the opinion of a practitioner with knowledge of the member’s medical condition, would subject the member to severe pain that cannot be adequately managed without immediate care or treatment. Note: If the above requirements are not met, the request for reconsideration will be considered under the standard fifteen (15) business day timeline. All standard and expedited pre-service requests for reconsideration of a benefit denial must be submitted in writing with supporting clinical information by fax to: Behavioral Health (outpatient): 208-387-6840 Behavioral Health (inpatient): 208-519-3960 Commercial and FEP: 208-331-7344 Pharmacy: 208-387-6969 QHP Authorizations and Referrals: 208-286-3583 Inpatient (commercial, FEP, QHP): 208-331-7326 3. Effect of denial of pre-service authorization reconsideration request If the initial pre-service determination is upheld, and you choose to render the services anyway, the post-service claim will be denied as not medically necessary. In-network providers will be held financially liable in the form of a contractual obligation, which will appear on their remittance advice, and may have post-service appeal rights under the terms of their provider contract. II. Post-Service Claim Inquiries There are two ways that you can submit a post-service claim inquiry. Follow the process below for the online post-service claim inquiry process for all questions about the processing of a claim, unless the claim is denied for an appealable reason that requires medical records for review. Claims denied for an appealable reason that will require medical records to determine medical necessity cannot be handled through the post-service inquiry process. For claims denied for this reason, refer to the Post-Service Claim Appeal section of this policy. Online post-service claim inquiry Submit post-service claim inquiries through the provider portal at providers.bcidaho.com , using one of the two options below: Option 1 Log into providers.bcidaho.com Hover over Eligibility and Claims and select Claim Status . Search for the claim in question and view your claim. Click the hyperlink on the option to “Click here to submit a question about this specific claim”. The system will auto-populate the appropriate fields with your office information. You may need to enter your contact number. Select the subject that reflects the reason for your inquiry and complete the description field with the details of your question. You may attach any relevant files you would like reviewed, except medical records, corrected claims or explanation of benefits (EOBs). Medical records can only be submitted with a first- or second-level appeal . Corrected claims, resubmissions, or replacement claims need to be submitted as corrected or replacement claims as outlined in PAP206 . Select Submit . Your submission will be securely delivered to the appropriate department at Blue Cross of Idaho following Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) compliance guidelines. An automated confirmation of your inquiry submission with the case number will be sent to the email address associated with your portal login. Please save this for your records. A representative from Blue Cross of Idaho will review and respond to your request in one of the following ways: Adjustment of claim in question if appropriate. In this case, the new remit with adjusted claim information is considered your inquiry response. If the claim cannot be adjusted, a detailed explanation of the review will be sent to the email address associated with your portal login.
